From: Bethany Henderson <[REDACTED]> 
Sent: Wednesday, 11 March, 2026 17:22
To: John Black <[REDACTED]>; Jillian Burkley <[REDACTED]>; Anubav Vasudevan <[REDACTED]>; S Johnson <[REDACTED]>; Tom Sabo <[REDACTED]>; Adriana Palacios <[REDACTED]>; Tina Beaty <[REDACTED]>; Thomas Colvin <[REDACTED]>; David Berol <[REDACTED]>; [REDACTED]
Cc: Jerrod Anderson <[REDACTED]>
Subject: school board liaison update
Importance: High

Happy Wednesday,

On behalf of myself and Jerrod, I want to thank all of you again for the extraordinary amount of intentionality, time, and effort each of you are putting into this committee's work. It's such a privilege to attend committee meetings as your liaisons and observe the robust and thoughtful discussions. As we're now roughly at the halfway point of the committee's efforts (gulp!), we wanted to provide a couple of clarifications and updates that we hope will help as you continue your collective efforts:

1) We wanted to remind everyone that this committee does NOT need to (and is not expected to) provide the Board a fully drafted proposed policy nor even committee-agreed-upon specific phrasing for suggested policy components. Writing the actual policy language is the Board's constitutional responsibility.

The Board is looking to this committee first and foremost to inform us by providing recommendations on what content the policy should include along with what considerations it should address or (de)prioritize, and why. In other words, your core charge is to provide the Board a roadmap, guidance, and information about any trade-offs; the Board's job is to choose the trade-offs and write the ultimate policy language.

Consequently, the committee does NOT need to be unanimous on all of the recommendations it presents to the Board. We want your (as representatives of the broader community's) collective best thinking and ideas. Therefore, in the report the committee will make to the full Board on April 28, if the committee has unanimous or supermajority consensus recommendations or language, certainly tell us those. If the committee has collectively identified concepts or content that it deems important, but on which members have strongly differing opinions, please tell us those, too, and share the different perspectives so that the full Board can weigh them.

2) We know this is a wildly rapid process for a BIG subject. The good news is that this first FCCPS AI policy is not a one-and-done. With the tech so quickly evolving, it will be important for the Board to revisit and update the AI policy on a regular basis -- allowing for continuous improvement. If the committee collectively has recommendations on frequency of review (e.g. annually, every 2 years, etc...) it would be very helpful to incorporate those recommendations and rationale (or considerations and trade-offs of different intervals) in the final report to the Board.

We know the weight all of you feel in doing this important work, and are immensely grateful for your time, energy, and brainpower. Our community is lucky to have you!

With gratitude,
Bethany

Bethany Rubin Henderson
FCCPS School Board Member 2024 - 2027
